standard.title: Apply target language sound system
standard.description: apply features of the target language sound system, including pitch, rhythm, stress, pronunciation and intonation, and show how these are represented in familiar and some unfamiliar contexts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can recognise and use features of the target language sound system including vowels, consonants, intonation and stress in familiar contexts (AC9LS8EU01). They have not yet applied these features independently in unfamiliar contexts or reflected on regional pronunciation variation across target language communities.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students apply features of the target language sound system — including pitch, rhythm, stress, pronunciation and intonation — in familiar and some unfamiliar spoken contexts, and demonstrate understanding of how these are represented in the writing system, including awareness of regional variation.

nodes.label: Accurate and fluent pronunciation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can produce target language sounds, stress and intonation with sufficient accuracy and consistency to be understood in familiar and some unfamiliar contexts.
nodes.minimum_width: Demonstrate accurate production of the key phonological features of the target language (vowels, target consonants, stress patterns) in a prepared spoken text.
nodes.typical_width: Apply accurate pronunciation, stress and intonation across prepared and semi-prepared spoken tasks; use phonological knowledge to support pronunciation of unfamiliar words; apply correct terminology for phonological features and marking conventions.
wider: Record and critically review own spoken production — identify specific phonological features to improve and practise targeted correction
Research and compare pronunciation across two or more regional varieties of the target language — discuss what the variation reveals about language change and cultural identity

response_modes.reason: Phonological accuracy at Y9-10 is primarily a fluency issue — students have learned the rules but need continued practice to maintain accuracy under communicative pressure. Performance tasks with self-assessment and recording support the ongoing consolidation this requires.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Regional pronunciation variation is both a linguistic and intercultural topic at Y9-10 — understanding that the target language is spoken differently across communities challenges the notion of a single 'correct' model and deepens intercultural understanding.
success_criteria: Produces a prepared spoken text with consistent and accurate vowel sounds, target consonants and sentence stress
Can apply phonological knowledge to attempt pronunciation of an unfamiliar word in the target language

nodes.label: Intonation, rhythm and communicative meaning
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use pitch, rhythm and intonation to convey communicative meaning — distinguishing mood, emphasis and intention in spoken target language production.
nodes.minimum_width: Demonstrate at least two distinct intonation patterns that convey different communicative meanings (e.g. certainty vs doubt, statement vs question, excitement vs neutrality) in the target language.
nodes.typical_width: Use pitch, rhythm and intonation to convey mood, emphasis and communicative intent; recognise and reproduce intonation patterns from authentic audio sources; identify how intonation affects the meaning of target language utterances.
wider: Analyse the use of pitch, rhythm and intonation in target language audio or video texts intended for different purposes (advertisement, news, narrative, conversation) — identify how prosodic features serve each purpose
Practise prosodic features through performance texts (poems, songs, speeches) and reflect on how prosody shapes audience response

response_modes.reason: Intonation as a meaning-making resource is only apparent across varied communicative purposes. Exposure to target language texts across multiple genres and registers allows students to observe how prosodic choices serve different communicative ends.

success_criteria: Produces at least two spoken utterances with audibly different intonation patterns conveying different communicative meanings
Can identify how intonation shifts meaning in at least one heard example from a target language audio source
